en-US.author: Jean-Pierre Bergamin
en-US.description: CLI for exploring and managing Markdown knowledge bases with YAML frontmatter
en-US.longDescription: Hyalo is a fast command-line tool for searching, filtering, and mutating collections of Markdown files with YAML frontmatter. It supports property queries, tag filtering, regex search, wikilink tracking, and bulk metadata updates. Compatible with Obsidian vaults, Zettelkasten systems, and any structured Markdown documentation.
en-US.name: hyalo
en-US.releaseNotes:
Upgrading from 0.25.x - Rebuild your index once. The snapshot format is now 12 (0.25.1 wrote 7). An existing .hyalo-index is refused with a warning, and the command falls back to disk, until you run hyalo create-index. - Several breaking changes, each marked Breaking below: the reader skips raw HTML, $$ math and code elements; a dry run exits 0; an invalid lint severity is refused; init/deinit protect your .hyalo.toml; new --file names a note. - Highlights: bulk writes survive power loss (every note ends up whole, old or new). lint is about a third faster on large vaults (MDN: 4.97 s to 3.24 s). A create-index that changed nothing is about 30% faster and uses about 57% less memory. New opt-in [links] redirect_property setting. [0.26.0] - 2026-11-09 Added - find --fields links tells an ambiguous link from a missing one. A bare [[stem]] that names two or more notes, or an alias two notes claim, carries ambiguous: true and candidates (sorted, vault-relative, identical on a disk scan and under --index); no other link carries either key. Text mode prints (ambiguous: a/note.md, b/note.md) in place of (unresolved). The link is still broken, so find --broken-links, summary.links.broken and HYALO006 count it as before (DEC-374). - lint --fix over 200 or more files prints lint --fix: N/M files on stderr every 200 files and lint --fix: M/M files, done at the end, like the other bulk write phases; -q silences it (DEC-383). - links fix and mv read a link target one way (DEC-384): a path suffix names a note ([[x/note]] for a/x/note.md; two notes sharing it are ambiguous) and [[./x]]/[[../x]] are relative to the source folder, so an in-vault ../x is no longer out_of_vault. - [links] redirect_property = "redirect_from" (unset by default, no flag) resolves a site-absolute link ([x](/old/url), [[/old/url]]) to the note that lists that URL path under the property, as a last resort after every file, directory-index, stem and alias match, so a real file always wins. The link carries via: "redirect" and is a graph edge; a path two notes list is ambiguous (DEC-374); links fix rewrites no target for such a link (a broken #fragment still gets the usual anchor repair against the declaring note) and mv leaves it alone, and a file created or moved onto a claimed path takes over the links that resolved through the claim. A value with a #fragment or ?query names part of a page and is ignored. On GitHub Docs it resolves 5,535 of the 6,082 broken markdown links (broken links 7,406 to 1,871; 237 of those now report a broken #anchor). --index builds the map from the properties a snapshot already holds, so changing the setting needs no rebuild and no format bump. hyalo config reports links.redirect_property; a blank name is a config error like an invalid lint severity (the gates refuse; DEC-415). Changed - Faster, with identical answers: a create-index rerun that changed nothing now decides so before it decodes the search postings, clones the entries or resolves the link graph (DEC-414). On MDN's 14,375 notes the no-op takes about 25% less wall time (22.6% and 27.8% in two interleaved sets on a busy machine), 41% less CPU and less than half the memory (526 MB to 226 MB); the result and the untouched snapshot are byte-identical, and a rerun that does change something is level. A no-op no longer re-validates the postings beyond their MessagePack framing, so a torn or truncated snapshot still rebuilds, while a single damaged byte that leaves the framing intact is left alone: the three warnings about an unreadable or invalid BM25 section now end with "hyalo create-index --force rebuilds it". - Faster, with identical answers: the per-file drift check that unscoped or graph-reading --index reads (find, backlinks, summary) run, drifted or not (DEC-302), now calls stat once per indexed file instead of twice, about 0.02 s less system time on MDN's 14,375 notes. - Breaking: the reader skips raw HTML, $$ math and code-like elements.
